header.author: Temple library papyri

notes.1.66: Line 66: sḫw 'striking' and nh (rendered 'terror') are uncertain; the clause is obscure. Line 68: wꜣḏ-n-Sḫm,t, 'the green (papyrus?) of Sekhmet', seems to be an amulet or plant, like the sycamore in the preceding line; tm n ꜥnḫ, 'completion of life', is uncertain. Line 69: sk.pl, 'destroyers', is uncertain.
notes.1.83: Rrj.t is the sow or hippopotamus goddess Reret, here in the plural.
notes.1.203: A list of gods receiving offerings. Setwy, Pedj-aha, Iun, 'the Body of the Jackals' (H̱,t-sꜣb.pl) and 'Nekhen of the King' are uncertain readings or unidentified figures; Iunet may be Dendera.
notes.1.212: Iq and Nebyt are unidentified places. Wepetawy ('he who divides the Two Lands') and Wadj are uncertain as names. The Setep-sa is the royal palace.

nodes.text: Sekhmet is on his head, the Powerful One at his forehead, her striking in her fury, her terror evil in her own secret form.
The Eye of Ra protects Pharaoh, may he live, prosper and be healthy, a god keen is he.

Horus, Horus! The green-of-Sekhmet around the flesh of Pharaoh, may he live, prosper and be healthy; the completion of life given to Pharaoh, may he live, prosper and be healthy, for his flesh, as he appears as Nefertem.
No destroyers of Sekhmet will be against him, no slaughterers of Bastet will be against him.
Stand up, stand up, great Reret-goddesses! Sit down, sit down, divine Reret-goddesses!

For the Falcon of Horus, the Souls of Pe, Isis-Hesat, Meret of Upper Egypt, Horus of Iunet, Anubis, Setwy, Pedj-aha, Iun, Thoth, Bat, Serqet, the West, Neith, Wadjet, Wepwawet of Upper Egypt, the Body of the Jackals, Nekhen of the King.

For Weret-hekau, Maat, Ptah South-of-his-Wall, Shu, Tefnut, Geb, Nut, Osiris, Isis, Nephthys, Herishef, Sobek of Shedet, Horus lord of Letopolis, Min of Coptos, Hathor lady of Iq, Hathor lady of Tepihu, Wadjet, Wepetawy, Wadjet lady of Nebyt, Hathor lady of the Sycamore, Hathor lady of Sekhet-Ra, the Gods of the Setep-sa, Wepwawet, Wadj, Horus-Mekhentienirty, [...]
